digest.component_or_area: completion verifier context assembly and recovery
propositions: The completion verifier spends 67-82% of its file-fetch requests re-reading files already declared in ticket file_impact, causing runaway loops dominated by search_files repeats and extending wall-clock cost by 84-158 requests per run.

Prefetching the closing ticket's declared file_impact contents (own set only on graph=False close path, or subtree union on graph=True deep-review path) into a labelled, bounded section of the assembled context reduces discovery-dominated baseline request counts by at least 20% while maintaining equal verdict class.

The prefetch mechanism must honour the close gate's graph=False boundary (own file_impact only, no subtree walk), remain opt-in to assemble_context (default None for generic review callers to stay byte-identical), and ride the existing automatic message-tail cache via the byte-stable fenced ticket_context.

Oversized prefetch sections must be trimmed (skeleton-compress large files, then drop lowest-ranked paths) to fit within a 30k-token aggregate budget, with bytes included in physical_context_ceiling accounting so trimmed prefetch shrinks recovery context rather than raising an overflow error.

Anti-anchoring trust guidance stating that full prefetched bodies are directly usable but skeleton-marked files require re-read must live in the completion_verifier.md static system prompt BEFORE the volatile marker so it is inherited by both primary verifier and batched recovery successor prompts from a single source.

Phase-0 usage logging records raw distinct fetch lists (tool name + path) per gate run to measure post-clamp coverage, with close-path own-file_impact coverage at 29-33% of baseline reads and graph=True subtree-union coverage pinned against the synthetic e369 112-path fixture.
